newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTION FOCUS - Oil shares seen bullish.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTION FOCUS - Oil shares seen bullish.

text.p: The oil sector looks to be among the hottest group in the stock market near-term, with option activity signalling that the general public had yet to jump on the bull run, option analysts said.
The American Stock Exchange's oil stock index .XOI broke out of a 353-358 two-week range on Tuesday and extended gains today to touch a new intraday high of 363.11.

But a lack of open interest accumulation in out-of-the- money call options showed that the "slow money" had not yet joined the latest run up, said Todd Salamone, a senior research analyst at Cincinnati-based Investment Research Institute.
"Because we're seeing that lack of enthusiasm...that implies short-term there may be further upside as people continue to catch up," he said.
Salamone liked Chevron, Texaco and British Petroleum. He said Chevron, currently at 64-3/8, had potential to reach 70 in the next two months and Texaco, currently at 93-3/4, to 100.
Analysts noted that besides the impressive stock price performances, crude oil prices were on a bullish trend, which usually meant many oil firms would enjoy wider profit margins.
"I think oil stocks have begun another strong leg to the upside," said Bob Dickey, a managing director of Dain Bosworth Inc. He said the bull trend could last for six to 12 months.
Dickey noted that maturity would be an important factor in riding the wave with options.
"After yesterday's rally, it would be very normal for them to move sideways for another week or two," he said. "I'd want to make sure my options went at least two months out."
Dickey saw the XOI index's trading range in the past few weeks as consolidation after breaking out of a six-month range on September 11.
He projected 375 as an intermediate-term target for the XOI.
"This could be a bigger and longer-lasting trend than people think, so I think you'd want to have a long option to take as much advantage of it as possible," Dickey added.
Dickey said domestic oil firms had the greatest potential from a cycle perspective, and added that he liked Unocal Corp and Marathon Oil.
